_comment: Intended toolkit-vs-runtime skill differences. Written by `scripts/skill_drift.py --declare`; each entry is pinned to both copies' fingerprints and goes stale when either side changes.

avoid-ai-writing.reason: Size racket: runtime's local-addition section cross-references ../manuscript-pipeline/writing_voice.md, a runtime-only sibling skill path; toolkit instead ships its own check-style.js tool. SKILL.md is grandfathered oversized per the 260903 user decision (memory: project_scitoolkit_shared_script_fork_260903) and not to be split.

conda-env-manager.reason: Reverse-direction: toolkit is ahead. Toolkit's Step 3.5 and Related-skill section reference skills/compat-check, a toolkit-only skill absent from the runtime tree, so the runtime copy cannot receive this content until compat-check itself is ported there.

experiment-hub.reason: License: the runtime copy is Proprietary and the toolkit ships MIT. No runtime content may be ported; the toolkit copy is maintained independently.

generate-image.reason: Toolkit is ahead: runtime Related Skills still names scientific-slides and latex-posters, which the toolkit does not ship (it routes to journal-ppt and publication-figures instead), and the toolkit script carries the Windows UTF-8 stdout fix the runtime lacks.

paper-extract.reason: Env-dependence: runtime SKILL.md points its Script Location at ~/.claude/scripts/extract_paper_assets.py (the maintainer's personal layout, 260904 audit), while the toolkit ships its own self-contained copy under skills/paper-extract/scripts/ so a distribution install works standalone.

patent-invention-disclosure.reason: Env-dependence: the runtime addition documents a Stop hook (hooks/patent_qc_gate_stop.sh wired into the maintainer's own stop_hook.sh, 260912) that only exists in that person's Claude Code settings.json wiring, not something a toolkit distribution install has or can port.

primer-design.reason: License: the runtime copy is Proprietary and the toolkit ships MIT. No runtime content may be ported; the toolkit copy is maintained independently.

statsmodels.reason: Reverse-direction: toolkit is ahead here, not lagging. Toolkit added references/model_selection.md (AIC/BIC, R-style formulas, CV caveats) after the runtime copy was last touched; nothing to port from runtime, the addition should go the other way eventually.
